Here's how to do it with your setup.

## 1. Annotate tests with `[Trait]`

Use the `[Trait("Category", "Integration")]` attribute from xUnit:

```csharp
using Xunit;

namespace MyApp.Tests;

public class OrderTests
{
    [Fact]
    public void Total_IsComputed() => Assert.True(true);      // no category — unit test

    [Fact]
    [Trait("Category", "Integration")]
    public void Order_PersistsToDatabase() => Assert.True(true);  // integration test
}
```

You can also apply `[Trait]` to the whole class to categorize all tests in it.

## 2. Run only Integration tests

Because your project has `TestingPlatformDotnetTestSupport=true`, `dotnet test` routes through **Microsoft.Testing.Platform**. Pass the filter after `--`:

```shell
dotnet test -- --filter "Category=Integration"
```

The `--` separates `dotnet test` arguments from MTP runner arguments. The filter expression `Category=Integration` matches the trait key/value pair you set.

To **exclude** integration tests (i.e., run only unit tests):

```shell
dotnet test -- --filter "Category!=Integration"
```

> **Note:** The `--filter` before `--` (the classic VSTest syntax) does *not* work with `TestingPlatformDotnetTestSupport=true`. Always use the `-- --filter` form with MTP.
